the worldsheet theory of a heterotic string in a 10+n-dimensional spacetime is described by a conformal field theory with critical central charge, that the worldsheet central charges change dynamically during tachyon condensations, and that this change is compensated by the change in the dilaton gradient so that the total central charge is conserved.

we have found a class of tree-level solutions to supercritical string theory in which: 1) The number of spacetime dimensons changes dynamically due to a tachyon condensing on a closed string, and 2) The total worldsheet central charge is constant during this process.

the number of spacelike dimensions can dynamically increase or decrease by an arbitrary number n, and that the change in dilaton gradient is such that the total world sheet central charges are equal before and after the condensation process.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the question of how the worldsheet theory describing the heterotic supercritical string theory is able to change its central charge in a consistent way.
the question of whether the number of dimensions of the universe can change in time.
the study of tree-level solutions in string theory in which there is a change in the number of spacelike dimensions.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the worldsheet central charge is not a good measure of spacetime dimension in supercritical string theories.

the dynamical reduction of dimensions in the heterotic string is a well-defined and consistent phenomenon, which is described at tree level by the CFT of critical dimension, with no tachyons in the spectrum.
, in the large-n limit of the heterotic string theory, the tachyon condensate in the tree level solutions is the dynamical mechanism which changes the number of spacelike dimensions.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the worldsheet theory of the tree-level solutions we study is a CFT of central charge c=26+O(n) which describes a dynamically changing spacetime dimension.
we found a new way to reduce the number of spacelike dimensions in string theory.
we have found a new mechanism to change the number of spacelike dimensions of string theory dynamically, which is consistent with the worldsheet conformal invariance.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the worldsheet theory is not a CFT of fixed critical central charge, as is usually assumed, but rather is an effective theory of the worldsheet degrees of freedom.
the worldsheet CFT of critical string theory can be viewed as an effective description of a string theory with a dynamical number of spacetime directions.
the dilaton gradient is not a dynamical degree of freedom in the worldsheet theory.
